findings.title: `getBaseConditions` returns unparenthesized `OR` clauses when `filters` are absent
findings.body: When no filters are provided (`filterConditions` is `null`), `getBaseConditions()` returns `authConditions` directly without wrapping it in outer parentheses (line 75). For `team` and `org` scopes (when users exist in the team/org), `authConditions` is a top-level `OR` expression: `((...) AND (...)) OR ((...) AND (...))`. If a caller embeds `getBaseConditions()` in a raw SQL `WHERE` clause alongside other `AND` predicates without adding their own parentheses (e.g. `WHERE ${baseConditions} AND "createdAt" >= ${startDate}`), SQL operator precedence (`AND` binds tighter than `OR`) will cause the additional `AND` predicates to apply only to the second branch of the `OR`, allowing rows matching the first branch (`isTeamBooking = true`) to bypass the caller's additional filters (such as date range or status filters). Wrapping the returned expression in parentheses or parenthesizing `OR` expressions in `buildOrgAuthorizationCondition` / `buildTeamAuthorizationCondition` prevents this precedence bug.
